com-ga-hoi-an.name: Hoi An chicken rice
com-ga-hoi-an.description: Fragrant yellow rice with chicken broth served with shredded chicken, Vietnamese coriander and mildly sour carrot and papaya salad; A typical dish of Hoi An.
com-ga-hoi-an.serving_basis: 4 plates of rice; about a quarter of a raw chicken including the bones per person.
com-ga-hoi-an.finished_dish: The golden rice grains are fragrant with the scent of turmeric and chicken broth, eaten with tender chicken, Vietnamese coriander and crispy sweet and sour salad.
com-ga-hoi-an.serving: Serve hot rice with shredded chicken, salad and a cup of broth. Season with fish sauce, pepper or chili according to taste.
com-ga-hoi-an.time_note: Total time includes operation and waiting time; Actual time depends on the kitchen and the size of the ingredients.
tips: Use enough chicken broth so that the rice is cooked through, not mushy.
Let the chicken cool down before shredding so that the meat fibers are neat and don't burn your hands.
The salad is only mixed with laksa leaves close to the time of eating to maintain freshness.

preparation_steps: Clean and drain chicken; lightly wash rice. Slice the onion thinly, soak in cold water to reduce its sharpness and then drain.
Grate papaya and carrot, mix vinegar with a little sugar and salt; Let it soak while cooking rice.
Wash coriander and lettuce and drain; Chop garlic, prepare turmeric powder.
cooking_steps: Boil the chicken in a pot of water with salt and a portion of turmeric powder until cooked; Take it out and let it cool, reserving the boiling water.
Sauté the garlic with oil, add the rice and stir gently until the seeds are firm; Cook with chicken broth according to the amount of water appropriate to the type of rice.
Tear or slice the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Mix chicken with onions, coriander and a little fish sauce, vinegar, and pepper; Mix papaya and carrot salad and taste the sweet and sour taste.
Compress the rice into a dome on a plate, arrange the chicken and salad next to it; Serve with lettuce and a cup of hot chicken broth.

nem-nuong-chay-hoi-an.name: Hoi An vegetarian grilled spring rolls
aliases: Hoi An vegetarian grilled spring rolls
nem-nuong-chay-hoi-an.description: Grilled fragrant vegetarian spring rolls, served with raw vegetables, pickles, rice paper rolls and a bowl of mildly spicy sweet and sour vegetarian sauce.
nem-nuong-chay-hoi-an.finished_dish: Hot vegetarian spring rolls, golden brown on the outside, chewy and soft on the inside; Herbs and pickles create a balanced grilled taste.
nem-nuong-chay-hoi-an.serving: Roll spring rolls with vegetables, cucumber and pickles in rice paper; dipping in vegetarian sauce. Use immediately while the spring rolls are still hot.
nem-nuong-chay-hoi-an.time_note: Total time includes operation and waiting time; Actual time depends on the kitchen and the size of the ingredients.
tips: Squeeze the vegetarian slices thoroughly so that the mixture is not mushy.
Soak bamboo skewers before grilling to limit burning.
Check the label of vegetarian slices and vegetarian fish sauce if needed to ensure veganism.

preparation_steps: Soak the vegetarian pork slices according to package instructions, squeeze thoroughly, then tear or chop.
Mix vegetarian slices with flour, tapioca starch, lemongrass, soy sauce, sugar, pepper and a spoonful of oil until sticky; let rest 15 minutes.
Wash vegetables, slice cucumber; Prepare pickles. Mix vegetarian fish sauce with lemon juice, filtered water, sugar and chili.
cooking_steps: Divide the mixture into bite-sized portions and shape it around soaked bamboo skewers; Press gently to make the spring roll adhere firmly.
Steam the spring rolls for about 8 minutes to shape, let cool, then brush with a thin layer of oil.
Grill on a grill pan, oven or air fryer over medium heat, turning evenly until the spring rolls are golden brown and hot through the center.
Serve spring rolls with raw vegetables, cucumber, pickles, rice paper and vegetarian dipping sauce. Roll right before eating.

bun-bo-hue-chay.name: Vegetarian Hue beef noodle soup
aliases: Hue style vegetarian beef noodle soup
bun-bo-hue-chay.description: Large bowl of vermicelli noodles in fragrant lemongrass vegetable broth, vegetarian satay and vegetarian pork floss; Eat with tofu, mushrooms, vegetarian rolls and herbs.
bun-bo-hue-chay.serving_basis: 4 bowls of noodle soup; The formula uses entirely plant ingredients.
bun-bo-hue-chay.finished_dish: Mild orange-red broth, fragrant with lemongrass and vegetables; Chewy noodles, mushrooms and tofu absorb flavor, and accompanying vegetables maintain freshness.
bun-bo-hue-chay.serving: Serve hot with raw vegetables, banana ears and lemon. Adjust the vegetarian satay separately to control spiciness.
bun-bo-hue-chay.time_note: Total time includes operation and waiting time; Actual time depends on the kitchen and the size of the ingredients.
tips: Only use vegetarian fish sauce and vegetarian seasoning; Check labels to avoid spices with animal ingredients.
Stew the vegetables over low heat and skim the foam to clear the broth.
Add the satay a little at a time because the spiciness of chili and satay are different.

preparation_steps: Wash and soak shiitake mushrooms until soft; Sliced ​​tofu, sliced ​​vegetarian patties. Prepare corn, radish, cassava and pineapple and cut into pieces.
Crush the lemongrass and partially chop it; Minced garlic and purple onion. Wash water spinach, bean sprouts, banana ears and herbs and drain.
Pick out the shiitake mushrooms and keep the filtered soaking water separate. Quickly boil vermicelli according to package instructions.
cooking_steps: Add water with corn, radish, cassava, pineapple, onion if any and mushroom soaking water into the pot; Simmer for about 30 minutes, skim foam and strain or keep vegetables as desired.
Pan-fried golden tofu. Fry garlic, shallots, and minced lemongrass with cashew oil; Add chili and vegetarian shrimp paste, stir until fragrant and then mix into the pot of broth.

Stir-fry straw mushrooms and shiitake mushrooms with a little vegetarian seasoning; Add mushrooms, vegetarian patties and tofu to the broth, cook for another 5 minutes. Season with rock sugar and vegetarian seasoning to taste.
Put vermicelli in a bowl, pour hot broth and toppings; Served with bean sprouts, split water spinach, banana ears, herbs and lemon.

mi-quang-chay-hoi-an.name: Hoi An Vegetarian Quang Noodles
mi-quang-chay-hoi-an.description: Quang yellow and turmeric noodles are served with a moderate amount of vegetable broth, tofu, mushrooms, raw vegetables, peanuts and crispy rice paper.
mi-quang-chay-hoi-an.serving_basis: 4 bowls of mixed noodles; The amount of water is less than that of noodle soup.
mi-quang-chay-hoi-an.finished_dish: Turmeric yellow noodles have a thin layer of broth rich in mushrooms and vegetables, served with raw vegetables, roasted peanuts and sesame rice paper.
mi-quang-chay-hoi-an.serving: Mix the noodles while still hot, break the rice paper into each bite to keep it crispy.
mi-quang-chay-hoi-an.time_note: Total time includes operation and waiting time; Actual time depends on the kitchen and the size of the ingredients.
tips: Hoi An Quang noodles use little broth; Cook just enough to coat the topping and soften the fibers.
Drain the vegetables and noodles before placing them in bowls so the broth doesn't dilute.
Use vegan broth and soy sauce; Don't add regular fish sauce.

che-bap-hoi-an.name: Hoi An corn sweet soup
che-bap-hoi-an.description: Cam Nam sticky corn sweet soup, soft and supple corn kernels in a light layer of water; Add a little coconut milk when serving.
che-bap-hoi-an.finished_dish: Fragrant soft corn kernels in light, sweet tea; Coconut milk adds fat but doesn't overpower the corn flavor.
che-bap-hoi-an.serving: Serve warm or cool; Drizzle with coconut milk right before eating to preserve the aroma and consistency.
che-bap-hoi-an.time_note: Total time includes operation and waiting time; Actual time depends on the kitchen and the size of the ingredients.
tips: Prioritize Cam Nam young sticky corn if available; The naturally sweeter the corn, the less sugar it needs.
Mix tapioca starch with cold water first to avoid clumping.
Add sugar slowly and stop when the corn flavor is still clear.

preparation_steps: Peel the corn and wash it; Use a knife to thinly slice the corn kernels, keeping the pulp to cook fragrant water.
Mix tapioca starch with a little cold water until dissolved. Prepare rock sugar and coconut milk separately.
cooking_steps: Put the corn pulp in a pot of water, boil for about 15 minutes to get the sweetness, then remove the pulp.
Add corn kernels and pandan leaves to the pot, stir gently, and cook until the kernels are soft. Add rock sugar and a little salt, taste sweet.
Pour dissolved tapioca starch into a small stream, pouring and stirring until the tea thickens slightly; Turn off the stove.
Warm the coconut milk separately. Scoop the sweet soup into a bowl, add a spoonful of coconut milk when eating; Serve warm or cool.
